item.title: China men's football team ends losing streak
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
ZHAOQING, China -- China ended a losing streak with a 2-0 home victory over Malaysia in an international friendly here on Saturday, with Wang Yudong and Zhang Yuning scoring in the first half. China had lost three consecutive friendlies in last international window, suffering a 3-0 defeat to New Zealand in September before falling 5-0 to Palestine and 1-0 to Tajikistan in October. With most of its key players back in the squad, China made a positive start and took the lead in the 10th minute. Following a series of passes down the right flank, Lin Liangming delivered a cross into the penalty area, where 20-year-old forward Wang arrived at the far post to head home. China doubled its lead nine minutes later, when Wang Shangyuan sent a well-weighted ball over the Malaysian defense from midfield, and Zhang chipped the ball over the goalkeeper from inside the penalty area. Tensions flared between the two sides in first-half stoppage time. After reviewing the incident on VAR, the referee showed yellow cards to China assistant coach Zhou Ting and Malaysia defender Tan Jun Jin. China enjoyed 59 percent possession in the first half and registered six shots, two on target, while Malaysia managed three attempts without a shot on target. The Chinese head coach Shao Jiayi made seven substitutions during the second half, and the host's attacking threat diminished. Malaysia thought it had pulled a goal back in the 77th minute when Fergus Tierney capitalized on a defensive error by China. However, after another VAR review, the referee ruled out the goal for a foul in the build-up. China goalkeeper Li Hao made two crucial saves in the closing stages to preserve the clean sheet. In the 90th minute, Tierney was sent off after receiving a second yellow card for a foul, as China held on to secure a 2-0 victory. "The match was not easy. As a coach, whether looking at the process or the result, I am very satisfied with what the players showed. The league season has just ended and everyone is very tired. For them to generate such enthusiasm, passion and team spirit at this point in time is exactly what the Chinese team needs," Shao said at the post match news conference. The 46-year-old urged that the players still need to stay calm. "This victory is very important, but we have no reason to be overly optimistic. The opponents had nearly 20 players unavailable, yet they still possess certain strength -- this is the current reality of Asian football. We cannot take any team or any match lightly." The Chinese side will play against Bahrain next Tuesday. "We have only two days to recover before the next match, which is very difficult, but professional players must get used to and adapt to this kind of situation. I believe they can perform better in the next match," he added.

item.title: Australian workers' solidarity with China marked 88 years on
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Senior government, industry and community representatives gathered in Wollongong in Australia's New South Wales state on Nov 13 for the annual commemoration of an industrial action by port workers, whose sacrifices for global peace and the building of China-Australia ties continue to be lauded nearly nine decades later. The solemn event commemorated the Dalfram Dispute of 1938, when 180 wharf workers at Port Kembla in Wollongong refused to load a shipment of pig iron onto the steamship SS Dalfram, bound for Japan, on Nov 15. The workers had heard that the iron would be used to make weapons against China, which was fighting Japanese invaders. The protest soon involved unions and other workers in the region and beyond, stretching over 10 weeks and leading to a lockout of ships, with about 4,000 steelworkers laid off. It also had support from local residents, drawing attention at home and abroad.

item.title: Reps from 115 Fortune Global 500 to attend APEC CEO Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
SHENZHEN -- Representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade said Sunday. US companies make up the largest group among participating companies from economies other than China, accounting for nearly 20 percent of the total, said Li Qingshuang, vice-chairperson of the CCPIT, at a news conference. Heads of several international organizations, as well as leaders of business associations from the United States, Russia, Japan and other economies, will also attend the summit, Li said.

item.title: 12 leaders of APEC economies to attend APEC CEO Summit 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
SHENZHEN -- Twelve leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies will attend the APEC CEO Summit 2026, which is scheduled to be held from Nov 17 to 18 in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade said Sunday. Chinese President Xi Jinping, along with leaders from APEC economies Australia, Canada, Chile, China's Hong Kong, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam, will attend the summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or participate in panel discussions, said Li Qingshuang, vice-chairperson of the CCPIT, at a news conference.

item.title: Forever searching: A German's TCM journey to Henan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
At 20, a young German man named Wuming bought a one-way ticket to Henan, China. He never expected to put down roots here and find his calling in traditional Chinese medicine. He once read Jia Dao's poem For an Absent Recluse as a tale of regret. Today, he sees it differently: the journey matters more than the destination, and the answers we seek may already lie within us.

item.title: Bilibili Gaming puts Chinese esports back on top of the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
The victory of Bilibili Gaming (BLG) sparked widespread celebration across Chinese social media on Sunday, as fans celebrated the team's 3-1 triumph over South Korea's Gen.G in the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, ending a five-year wait for another world title for China's top domestic league, the League of Legends Pro League (LPL). The League of Legends World Championship is the game's premier annual international competition and one of the most prestigious events in global esports. Held at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, the grand final saw BLG lose the opening game before winning the next three to defeat Gen.G and lift the Summoner's Cup. The victory marked the LPL's return to the top of the global competition for the first time in the past five years since Edward Gaming (EDG) won the title in 2021. Capturing the emotion of the LPL's 1,834-day wait for another world title, BLG's official social media account shared a message to its supporters: "From repeatedly coming close to victory to standing together on the highest podium today … At last, we can shout it out together: We are world champions!" For BLG's players, the triumph was the culmination of years of pursuit and, for some, the chance to put past disappointments behind them. "Today is the happiest day of my life," BLG's top laner Chen Zebin, also known as Bin, wrote on Weibo after the victory. Mid laner Zhuo Ding, also known as Knight, said winning the worlds had long been his ultimate goal. Having finished runner-up in 2024, he described this year's title as a chance to make up for that disappointment and restore the LPL's standing. Knight also addressed doubts about his ability to overcome Gen.G's mid laner Jeong Ji-hoon, known as Chovy, in the final. "Before the match, many people didn't believe I could beat Chovy, or that BLG could beat Gen.G. Now, I've proved that I'm better than him and that BLG is the strongest," said Knight, who was named the final's Most Valuable Player. The championship run was notable not only for the trophy itself, but also for the opponents BLG overcame along the way. The team defeated all four representatives of South Korea's League of Legends Champions Korea (LCK) at this year's worlds: Hanwha Life Esports in the Swiss stage, Dplus KIA in the quarterfinals, T1 in the semifinals and Gen.G in the final. The semifinal victory over T1 was particularly significant. It ended the South Korean team's 13-series winning streak against LPL opponents in best-of-five matches at the World Championship, a record that had stood for years. The achievement drew reactions from across the esports community and beyond. Chinese esports commentator Wang Duoduo celebrated the result on social media, writing: "They did it. They made history! For the first time, an LPL team has defeated all four LCK representatives at the world championships. All the regrets of the past have become part of the road that brought them here." Chinese gymnast Zhang Boheng, the 2021 world all-around champion posted: "I was so excited! Staying up all night was worth it. … I'm just as excited as I would be if I had won a championship myself," he wrote, adding that he hoped to watch the worlds final in person next year. BLG's South Korean head coach Yang Dae-in, known as Daeny, pointed to the team's preparation and understanding of the game's latest patch as important factors behind its success. In a post-final interview, he said he believed BLG had been ahead in its analysis of the current version of the game, while the LCK teams were catching up. The victory also brought the tournament beyond the screens of fans watching at home. According to the organizers' event information, viewing activities were arranged at more than 300 cinemas in over 110 cities across China, with more than 2,000 screenings scheduled. In Hangzhou, two screening halls at one cinema, with a combined capacity of more than 500 seats, were almost full, according to media reports. Some screenings sold out soon after tickets went on sale. From social media celebrations to packed cinema screenings, BLG's victory became a shared moment for fans across the country as the team put LPL back on top of the world. tujiayi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Preparations for APEC Shenzhen meeting ready: officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
SHENZHEN -- Preparations for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, South China, are ready, local officials said at a press briefing on Saturday. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Nov 18 and 19, Wang Xi, deputy head of the provincial preparatory leading group, told the briefing. Wang said organizers had incorporated green practices, traditional Chinese and local Lingnan culture, and digital technologies into venue preparations and services. During the meeting week, Guangdong will offer 218 visitor sites and 43 routes, including two representative ones in Shenzhen. Organizers have upgraded key venues and conducted comprehensive rehearsals, and have arranged reception, accommodation, catering, transport, medical care and interpretation, as well as measures for communications, weather, public security, public health and city operations, Wang said. Shenzhen Mayor Li Yun said all venues and facilities were ready. The city has strengthened transport, power, communications and hotel services while minimizing inconvenience to residents' daily lives. The city has also introduced measures to make travel and daily transactions easier for visiting delegates. Dedicated channels for meeting representatives will be available at nine sea, land, air and rail ports. More than 100,000 foreign-language signs have been standardized, and over 7,000 AI translation devices have been installed at key locations. Taxis will provide bilingual announcements. More than 3,000 ATMs support cash withdrawal for foreign bank cards, while over 1,600 bank branches offer currency exchange. Shenzhen's metro fare gates will accept contactless payments with overseas bank cards. The city has also expanded its departure tax-refund program to 3,160 stores, including more than 1,000 offering instant refunds. Data released at the briefing also showed that Shenzhen has become the first city in the Chinese mainland to record more than 5 trillion yuan ($744.6 billion) in foreign trade. Shenzhen Customs said the city's imports and exports totaled 5.25 trillion yuan in the first 10 months of this year, up 40.9 percent year-on-year. Exports rose 19.7 percent to 2.71 trillion yuan, while imports surged 73.7 percent to 2.54 trillion yuan.
